Limitation
- I can’t access or edit your spreadsheet in this session: there’s no spreadsheet tool available and you haven’t pasted any rows. I therefore cannot open, inspect, or change the workbook. I will not claim the workbook was changed.

Concrete next step (pick one)
- Option A — I do it for you: enable a file upload or paste a representative sample (including header row and ~20 sample rows, showing any formula cells) so I can provide exact step-by-step edits or a small script you can run.
- Option B — You do it now with these safe, concrete steps (recommended). Make a backup copy of the workbook first, then follow the detailed steps below for Excel or Google Sheets depending on what you use. After you run them, paste any errors or a few sample rows and I’ll help adjust.

Recommended safe workflow (preserves formulas)
1) Backup
   - Save a copy of the workbook (File > Save As / Make a copy). Work on the copy.

2) Inspect & mark formulas (so you don’t accidentally overwrite them)
   - Excel: On the copy, press Ctrl+` (shows formulas). Note which columns are formula columns.
   - Google Sheets: View > Show formulas.
   - Alternatively, add a helper column to flag formula rows: =ISFORMULA(A2) (Excel/Sheets) and filter on FALSE to operate on data-only rows where possible.

3) Detect duplicates (without removing yet)
   - Add a helper column "IsDup" (row 2 formula example) that marks duplicates using the key columns that define a duplicate (adjust columns A and B):
     - Excel/Sheets: =COUNTIFS($A$2:$A$1000,$A2,$B$2:$B$1000,$B2)>1
   - Filter on IsDup = TRUE to review duplicates before removal.

4) Remove duplicates safely
   Option 1 — Non-destructive, recommended:
     - Create a deduplicated view on a new sheet so originals and formulas remain untouched.
     - Google Sheets / Excel 365: On a new sheet use UNIQUE:
       - =UNIQUE('RawSheet'!A1:Z1000) — this builds a deduplicated table (headers in row 1). Verify results, then copy values back if desired.
     - Excel (all versions): Use Power Query (Get & Transform):
       - Data > From Table/Range > in Power Query Editor select the columns that define uniqueness > Home > Remove Rows > Remove Duplicates > Close & Load to new sheet. This keeps the original file intact.
   Option 2 — If you must delete rows in place:
     - Work on the backup copy.
     - Filter to show duplicates (helper column) and delete rows you confirm are duplicates.
     - If formulas are per-row, after deleting rows, re-fill formulas down where needed (select the formula cell and drag/fill or use Table so formulas auto-propagate).

5) Identify and fix broken date formats
   Step A — Identify cells that are not true dates:
     - Add helper column "IsDate": =IF(A2="","",ISNUMBER(A2))  (TRUE if Excel/Sheets treats it as a date serial number).
     - Filter to IsDate = FALSE to see problem cells.
   Step B — Common fixes (do these in a helper column so originals are preserved until verified)
     - If dates are stored as text in recognizable formats (e.g., "01/02/2021" but treated as text):
       - Excel: use VALUE or DateValue in helper: =IF(A2="", "", VALUE(TRIM(A2))) or =IFERROR(DATEVALUE(TRIM(A2)), "")
       - Google Sheets: =IF(A2="", "", VALUE(TRIM(A2)))
       - Then format helper column as Date. Verify results before replacing original.
     - If dates are compact strings like "20200601" (YYYYMMDD):
       - Use parsing formula in helper: =DATE(LEFT(A2,4),MID(A2,5,2),RIGHT(A2,2))
     - If dates are ambiguous (dd/mm vs mm/dd) or locale mismatches:
       - Use Text to Columns (Excel) or split+rebuild (Sheets) to specify the correct order:
         - Excel: Select column > Data > Text to Columns > Delimited > Next > Next > Column data format: Date and choose DMY or MDY > Finish.
         - Sheets: Data > Split text to columns by delimiter, then use =DATE(year,month,day) to recombine in correct order.
     - If you have mixed formats, create a helper column that tries multiple parses and flags failures:
       - Example (Excel): =IFERROR(DATEVALUE(A2), IF(LEN(A2)=8, DATE(LEFT(A2,4),MID(A2,5,2),RIGHT(A2,2)), ""))

6) Replace originals only after verification
   - After helper column conversions look correct for a sample, copy the helper column, Paste Special > Values over the original date column (only after backup).
   - Reformat as Date using the desired date format.

7) Final checks
   - Sort by key columns to confirm duplicates removed and dates look correct.
   - Check dependent formulas (recalculate: F9 in Excel) and spot-check totals or counts.
   - If rows were deleted and formulas referenced absolute row ranges, update those ranges (or better: convert ranges to Tables so references are stable).

Short specific commands (Excel)
- Create backup: File > Save As
- Show formulas: Ctrl+`
- Text to Columns for date parsing: Data > Text to Columns > (navigate) > Column data format: Date (choose DMY/MDY)
- Remove duplicates (if you accept in-place deletion): Data > Remove Duplicates (select columns). Do this on the backup sheet.
- Power Query dedupe: Data > From Table/Range > Remove Duplicates in editor > Close & Load

Short specific commands (Google Sheets)
- Make a copy: File > Make a copy
- Show formulas: View > Show formulas
- UNIQUE dedupe: =UNIQUE(Sheet1!A1:Z)
- Detect text dates: =ISNUMBER(A2)
- Convert text to date: =VALUE(A2) or custom parse with DATE/LEFT/MID/RIGHT
- Split text to columns: Data > Split text to columns

If you want, next:
- Paste 10–20 sample rows (including header and showing some broken dates and some duplicates) and I will produce the exact formulas/Power Query steps you should run on your file. Or enable a file upload and I’ll give exact edits to perform (I still can’t change it myself until a tool is available).
